_note: This is a WORKLOAD PROFILE, not a proving report. It reuses the zkprof report schema's vocabulary for the fields it can fill and carries everything workload-specific in the documented x_workload extension block. Because the report schema is closed (additionalProperties:false), x_workload is a documented extension and a validator running on the report schema would flag it — expected, same pattern as W3.13's docs.

x_workload.source: AINumbers proving records, 2026-08-30 (supplied facts block; every number below traces to it)

system.constraint_scale_analog: user_cycles (risc0 is a zkVM, not a circuit; cycles are the constraint analog — not interchangeable with gates)

cycle_distribution.heavy_outlier_cause: in-guest secp256k1 ECDSA recovery (known crypto-in-guest cost cliff)

browser_prover_thresholds_derived.method: linear extrapolation from the supplied recent_batch points (derived/approximate, not a measurement)

cadence_tier_bound.note: 30M-cycle kernel at the derived cycles/s; the whole cadence-provable tier is on the order of 17-19 min per proof on the supplied GPU class

browser_prover_thresholds_derived.out_of_reach: the >30M downtime lane and especially the 839.7M ECDSA cliff (~1.5-2h on GPU) are out of reach for any prover slower than the existing GPU path

open_items: whether browser-side proving is a goal at all
the actual cadence window (the derived 17-19 min is an extrapolation, not a target)
